question: In order to avoid an accident with the vehicle in front while driving under normal condition, you should use the

options.text: Two- second rule.
Four- second rule.
Two metres rule.

notes: Source prints a space after the hyphen in 'Two- second' and 'Four- second'; kept as printed.

question: When being followed by a police vehicle with its siren on, you should

options.text: Accelerate quickly to get away from it.
Pull over safely, as soon as possible to let it pass.
Brake quickly and stop to let it pass.

question: When approaching a road that is flooded but passable to vehicles, you should

options.text: Engage a higher gear to go through the flood.
Engage a lower gear to go through the flood.
Drive through as fast as possible.

question: When driving along a two-way street, you should

options.text: Always keep near the centre line of the road.
Not cross the centre line at bends.
Not overtake at all times.

question: When turning right at a one-way street, you should position your vehicle

options.text: In the right hand lane.
Just left of the centre of the road.
In any lane depending on the traffic conditions.

question: When driving at night, dip your headlights

options.text: To light up the road immediately in front you.
So as not to dazzle drivers of oncoming vehicles.
To prolong the life of the car battery.

notes: Option A in source reads 'in front you' (missing 'of'); kept as printed.

question: When driving at night, you should use

options.text: Dipped headlight.
High beam.
Side lights only.

question: When should you use the right outer most lane of a carriageway?

options.text: When driving at the maximum speed.
When overtaking.
When all other lanes are occupied.

notes: Source prints 'outer most' as two words; kept as printed.

question: During bus lane prohibited hours, motorist is allowed to use the bus lane when

options.text: It is empty.
The other lanes are congested.
The driver is trying to avoid a collision.

question: A child is required to use a child restraint if the child is

options.text: 7 years old.
9 years old.
11 years old.

question: What does this sign mean?
picture: Blue circular sign with a white arrow going up and bending to the left

options.text: You must turn left ahead.
You are approaching a junction with a one-way street to the left.
Hazard ahead. Keep more to the left.

question: Which of these signs is a Mandatory Sign?

options.text: Blue circular sign with a white arrow pointing right
Blue square sign with a white expressway symbol (road passing under a bridge)
Red-bordered triangle sign with a black vertical line and a side road to the right

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop.

question: What does this sign mean?
picture: Red-bordered circular sign with the number 80 in black

options.text: Cannot drive slower than 80 km/h.
Cannot drive beyond 80 km/h.
Maintain your speed at 80 km/h.

question: Which of these signs prohibit you to turn left?

options.text: Red circle with a red diagonal slash over a black arrow bending to the right
Red circle with a red diagonal slash over a black arrow bending to the left
Blue circular sign with a white arrow bending to the left

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop. Question grammar ('prohibit you to turn') kept as printed.

question: Which of these signs is a warning sign?

options.text: Red-bordered upside-down triangle sign with the words "GIVE WAY"
Red-bordered triangle sign with a black broken circle (roundabout symbol)
Blue rectangular sign with a white arrow pointing left and the words "ONE WAY"

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop.

question: Which of these signs means 'lanes merging'?

options.text: Red-bordered triangle sign with a curved arrow angling in beside a straight upward arrow
Red-bordered triangle sign with one upward and one downward arrow side by side
Red-bordered triangle sign with two horizontal arrows, one pointing right and one left

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop.

question: Which of these signs means slow down, there is a series of bends ahead?

options.text: Red-bordered triangle sign with a single black road curving to the right
Red-bordered triangle sign with a skidding car and wavy tyre tracks
Red-bordered triangle sign with a black zigzag road line

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop.

question: Which of these signs means 'uneven road' ahead?

options.text: Red-bordered triangle sign with a single black hump on the road
Red-bordered triangle sign with two black bumps on the road
Red-bordered triangle sign with a skidding car and wavy tyre tracks

notes: Option signs are small thumbnails; descriptions made from an enlarged crop.

question: What does this sign means?
picture: White circular sign with a black border and a black bus symbol

options.text: Parking place for buses only.
Bus terminus ahead.
Bus stop.

notes: Source typo in question: 'What does this sign means?'; kept as printed.

question: When you approached this traffic sign, you should
picture: Blue square expressway symbol sign crossed out by a red diagonal line

options.text: Speed up to merge with traffic on the expressway.
Slow down as you are leaving the expressway.
Stop and make a U-turn as road is ending.

notes: Question uses past tense 'approached' as printed.
